title: Computer Centre Management
description: Managing a computer centre: infrastructure, facilities, networks, security, support and budgets; the meaning, functions, roles and skills of management and the classical and human-relations theories; planning and objectives; organizing and staffing; leadership, motivation and communication; and IT projects and data-centre security and services. Built from the CSC 301 lecture note (Ayorinde) and the Principles of Management lectures; project costing and scheduling and data-centre security, which the outline and the 2023/24 paper cover, are added from general knowledge.

topics.title: Computer Centre Management and Planning
topics.summary: Computer centre management plans, organizes and coordinates resources so a computer or data centre gives reliable, secure and efficient services. Its planning covers strategy, infrastructure, security, disaster recovery, budgets, resources, training, compliance and communication.
subtopics: Infrastructure and facility management
Network management and system administration
Security, resource allocation and the service desk
Budgeting and financial management
Strategic, infrastructure and security planning
Disaster recovery, training, compliance and review

topics.title: The Meaning, Functions and Roles of Management
topics.summary: Management is the coordination of all resources through planning, organizing, directing and controlling to attain stated objectives. Managers play interpersonal, informational and decisional roles and need technical, human and conceptual skills.
subtopics: Definitions and characteristics of management
Management as an art and a science
Functions: planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling
Mintzberg's managerial roles
Technical, human and conceptual skills
The internal, market and macro environment

topics.title: Management Theories
topics.summary: Classical theory includes Taylor's scientific management, Fayol's 14 principles and Weber's bureaucracy. The human relations school of Elton Mayo, Schein's assumptions about people and McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y turned attention to people and their social needs.
subtopics: Taylor's scientific management
Fayol's administrative theory and 14 principles
Weber's bureaucracy and its weaknesses
Elton Mayo and the Hawthorne studies
Schein's four assumptions about people
McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y

topics.title: Planning and Objectives
topics.summary: Planning decides what objectives to accomplish, the actions to achieve them and who is responsible; it precedes every other function. Plans are strategic, tactical or operational; the planning process has eight steps; MBO links individual and organizational goals; and SWOT and PEST analyses inform strategy.
subtopics: Meaning and importance of planning
Strategic, tactical and operational plans; standing and single-use plans
Corporate, business and functional strategy; mission and objectives
The planning process
Management by objectives
Barriers to planning; SWOT and PEST

topics.title: Organizing and Staffing
topics.summary: Organizing creates a structure of roles through division of work, departmentation, coordination, chain and unity of command and span of control. Staffing fills positions with the right people through job analysis, recruitment, selection, training, appraisal and reward.
subtopics: Principles of organizing
Authority, power, responsibility and accountability; delegation
Functional, product, geographical and customer designs
Line and staff; centralization and span of control
Job descriptions, recruitment and selection
Training, appraisal, rewards and promotion

topics.title: Leadership, Motivation and Communication
topics.summary: Leadership is influencing people to strive willingly toward group goals, studied through trait, behavioural (autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire) and situational approaches. Motivation is explained by content theories (Maslow, Herzberg) and process theories (Vroom, Adams), and communication links it all.
subtopics: Meaning and importance of leadership
Trait and behavioural approaches; leadership styles
Managerial grid and situational models (Fiedler)
Maslow's hierarchy and Herzberg's two-factor theory
Expectancy and equity theories
Communication, its channels and barriers; groups and change

topics.title: IT Projects, Data-Centre Security and Services
topics.summary: IT projects are proposed, costed, scheduled with milestones, Gantt charts and activity networks, monitored and reported, with risks managed throughout. A data centre protects devices and data with encryption, RAID, salting and secure DNS, and buys services through SLAs and cloud models.
subtopics: Proposal writing and project costing
Milestones, deliverables, Gantt charts and activity networks
Monitoring, reviews, report writing and risk management
Security of laptops, labs and hosted data; RAID
AES-256, password salting and DNS cache poisoning
Service-level agreements; IaaS, PaaS and SaaS
